topics.title: Financial hold on your account
topics.answer: A financial hold usually means an outstanding balance or unpaid fee on your student account. Until it's cleared, myZou may block enrollment.
steps: Log into myZou and check Holds on your student account.
Pay the balance or set up a payment plan with the Cashiers Office if eligible.
Allow 1–2 business days for the hold to clear after payment posts.
Confirm registration access before your enrollment appointment.

topics.title: Advisor hold
topics.answer: An advisor hold means you need to meet with your academic advisor before you can register. This is common before each registration period.
steps: Find your assigned advisor in myZou or your school/college advising office.
Schedule an advising appointment (many units use MU Connect scheduling).
Bring your Stellic plan or course ideas to the meeting.
After the advisor releases the hold, verify in myZou that registration is unblocked.

topics.title: Getting ready for registration
topics.answer: Before your myZou enrollment window opens, most students need holds cleared, a course plan in Stellic, and their registration appointment time.
steps: Check myZou for holds and required tasks on MizzouOne.
Build your next-semester plan in Stellic (primary + backups).
Note your enrollment appointment date and time in myZou.
Register promptly when your appointment opens — popular sections fill quickly.

topics.title: Prerequisite example: CS 2270
topics.answer: In this prototype, CS 2270 (Database Systems) requires CS 2050 and MATH 2300 on your completed or in-progress record. Stellic enforces this during registration.
steps: Open Stellic and search CS 2270 — check the Requirements tab.
If a prereq is in progress this semester, you may need advisor permission.
If missing a course, add the prerequisite to a future semester plan.
Ask your advisor if a substitution or exception applies to your situation.

topics.title: Changing your major (prototype guidance)
topics.answer: Changing majors affects your degree audit in Stellic — some credits may count as electives instead of major requirements. Always talk to an advisor before switching.
steps: Compare degree requirements in Stellic for your current vs intended major.
Meet with an advisor in the school/college you want to enter.
Ask how completed courses transfer within your new audit.
Submit any formal major-change paperwork your college requires.

topics.title: Connecting with Mizzou alumni
topics.answer: Mizzou's official program is Mizzou Mentoring — students browse alumni mentor profiles and choose someone aligned with their goals. Handshake is another way to see where alumni work.
steps: Create a profile on Mizzou Mentoring and browse mentors in your field.
Prepare 3–5 questions (internships, day-in-the-life, industry entry).
Be respectful of their time — 20–30 minute virtual chats are common.
Follow up with a thank-you and stay in touch through LinkedIn if appropriate.
tips: What drew you to your current role after Mizzou?
What skills matter most in your first internship?
What would you do differently in your junior year?

topics.title: Jobs & internships at Mizzou
topics.answer: Handshake is Mizzou's primary platform for jobs, internships, career fairs, and employer events. The Career Center also offers Big Interview for mock interview practice.
steps: Activate and complete your Handshake profile with an approved resume.
Set job alerts for roles that match your major and interests.
RSVP to career fairs and employer info sessions on Handshake.
Use Big Interview to practice before real interviews.

topics.title: Off-campus housing
topics.answer: Mizzou's official off-campus housing marketplace lists approved properties with filters and commute info. Pathfinder's map layers campus with Columbia complexes for browsing.
steps: Browse listings on offcampus.missouri.edu with your budget and bed count.
Use Pathfinder's map to see neighborhoods and estimated walk time to campus.
Contact landlords to schedule tours.
Confirm lease dates align with the academic calendar before signing.

topics.title: Using Stellic
topics.answer: Stellic is Mizzou's degree planning tool — it shows requirements, lets you drag courses into semesters, and flags conflicts or missing prerequisites.
steps: Log in at stellic.missouri.edu with your Mizzou credentials.
Review your degree audit for remaining requirements.
Plan next semester with primary and backup courses.
Share your plan with your advisor before registration.

topics.title: MizzouOne required tasks
topics.answer: MizzouOne collects administrative tasks like immunization records and other onboarding requirements. Unfinished tasks can block registration.
steps: Open MizzouOne and go to Required Tasks for Students.
Complete any outstanding immunization or document uploads.
Check myZou holds after submitting — processing may take a few days.
Contact the relevant office listed on the task if you're stuck.
